source: Hausdorff, Gait in Parkinson's Disease v1.0.0, PhysioNet, DOI 10.13026/C24H3N. First trial from GaCo01 through GaCo12, the first twelve numbered control participants in the Ga cohort. Time and left/right total vertical force only.
target: Left total force in newtons. Analyze raw and separately the offline 6 Hz low-pass component (fourth-order Butterworth, forward/backward). The filtered component is an explicitly distinct estimand. No filter selection from outcomes.
split: Split each record into three non-overlapping contiguous thirds by row count. In each third split at gaps outside 8-12 ms. Resample each contiguous run linearly to exact 10 ms grid within its own boundaries. Filter within run, discard one second at each end and pool eligible anchors across runs, retaining at least 15 seconds per third. Never cross a gap or a third boundary.
calibrate: For each participant and target use only the first third to compute the scalar derivative energy from a degree-four local polynomial on +/-30 ms. Repeat +/-40 and +/-50 ms as sensitivity. The second-derivative residual is orthogonalized against intercept, current force and first derivative. Freeze all coefficients before scoring later thirds.
decision: Decision concerns two lags only, separately for raw and filtered targets. Primary h=tau=40 ms. Both later thirds must meet all conditions: RMS fitted displacement at least 1% of the contemporaneous mean measured bilateral load, >=5% of the target increment RMS, joint signed relative error <=25%. These author-chosen thresholds express numerical size, not clinical importance. At least six of the twelve enrolled participants must qualify for a group-level positive. Report newtons, separable comparator, all grids, and future prediction errors of first-third fits. No patient records or clinical inference.
